title: Day One
author: Krrsh, former captain of the Misery's Company
content:
They left me the terminal. That's almost funny.

I have rations for eight days if I'm careful. Suit air recycles if I stay in Section 6 and don't move around too much. The habitable sections are still pressurized. I can work with this.

I am going to find a way out of this.

I always find a way.

title: Day Three
author: Krrsh
content:
There are marks on the walls in Section 2.

I read them all.

The old ones are from the Imperial crew. I don't understand most of it — the Sindalian dialect is too corrupted. But I understand: 'do not open Section 3.'

The newer ones — those are from the Brotherhood's castoffs. There are names I recognize. Morev Kasht. The Hauler woman.

None of them made it.

I am not them.

title: Day Five
author: Krrsh
content:
I found the suit.

Good quality. Civilian model. The chest plate is gone — not cracked, not torn. Removed. Whatever did it took its time.

The suit was sized for a human. The acid marks are old. Twenty years, maybe more.

This is what they leave behind.

I have been thinking about the radio. The beacon in my suit is powerful enough to reach a ship in-system if the ship is already looking. But the system is dead. Nobody looks here.

I need to boost the signal.

I need to boost it enough that someone passing through picks it up.

title: Day Six
author: Krrsh
content:
I wired the suit communicator to the station dish.

Forty-five minutes. Section 4. I ran the whole way back.

I know what this means. I can't use the communicator anymore unless I go back to Section 4 and unplug it. And Section 4 is between me and the thing in Section 5.

I have been calling it a 'thing' this entire time.

I have been trying not to describe it because if I describe it I have to admit that I have seen it.

I have seen it.

It is large. It is fast. It does not make sounds that I can hear directly. But my suit radio produces static when it is close. I have started tracking it that way.

The static is my early warning system.

The static has been getting louder.

title: Day Eight
author: Krrsh
content:
I think boosting the beacon made things worse.

The static is constant now. I don't know if it can hear the dish transmitting or if it's something else. I don't know how it works. I don't know anything about it except what I have figured out hiding here in the dark.

But I think it is drawn to signals. I think the dish is pulling it toward Section 4 instead of Section 6.

I think I accidentally built myself a decoy.

If someone comes — when someone comes — they will dock near Section 4.

I don't know how to warn them.

I don't have a communicator anymore.

title: Day Eleven (Probably)
author: Krrsh
content:
I lost count for a while.

The rations are almost gone. I have been rationing the rationing. This is what I have come to.

Krrsh of the Misery's Company. Four turrets and a crew of eleven. Feared in three systems.

Hiding under a panel on a dead station, counting the last of his protein bricks.

The signal is still going out. Someone will come. Someone always comes for the castoffs — the Brotherhood's tradition is an invitation to rescue, they just don't know it.

The static is quieter tonight.

I do not know if that is good.

title: Final Entry — No Date
author: Krrsh
content:
If you are reading this and I am not here to explain it myself:

The thing in the vents is real. It is not the station settling. It is not a malfunction.

It hunts by heat and by life and by radio.

The dish in Section 4 is keeping it busy. Do not turn the dish off. Do not transmit from Section 4. Do not run — it is faster than you.

I don't know how to kill it. I only know how to hide from it.

If I am dead, I hid badly.

If I am alive, find me in Section 6. Behind the secondary wall panel. I will be the Vargr who looks very bad and owes you a very large favour.

Hurry. I am almost out of air again.
